Meeting header: 2025-06-11 16:00 PDT / Duration: ~62 minutes / Recording link: (omitted)

[00:00:00] Maya Patel (AE): Hey everyone—thanks for making time. Quick roll call? We'll try to keep this under an hour. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood inference team, and Liam is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:08] Liam Chen (SE): hi all, Liam here. happy to dig into the model tradeoffs and benchmarks.
[00:00:12] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: Ana here. leading the ML work at GlobalClinic.
[00:00:15] Mark Huang: Mark - eng.
[00:00:18] Sara Lopez: Sara - PM. Javier dialed in late, he'll join in a bit.

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Customer wants a 6-week POC to validate an open-model for multilingual clinical summarization and triage. Key asks: Spanish/Portuguese fidelity, clinical term recall, p95 latency < 300ms for single-turn, cost targets, and on-prem/VPC constraints for PHI. Discussed a shortlist including 8B-13B and ~40B open models, quantization and LoRA fine-tune strategy, and Dedicated vs Hosted deployment tradeoffs.

[00:02:10] Maya: ok Ana — can you walk us through the success criteria from your side? what would make the POC a win?
[00:02:22] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: Sure. There are three pillars. One: quality — we want entity/med-term recall >= 92% on our annotated set and summarization ROUGE-L around baseline +5. Two: latency — p95 ideally under 300ms for our typical 350 token request, p99 under 500 if possible. Three: cost/ops — cost per 1M tokens should be reasonable; if we can prove Dedicated or on-prem gives ~30-40% lower unit cost that helps procurement.
[00:03:05] Mark: also we need to ensure encryption at rest + KMS integration and audits for our compliance team.
[00:03:12] Javier (later): yeah SOC 2, SAML SSO are gating items.

[00:04:00] Liam: great. For workload sizing, can you confirm expected concurrency and tokens per request?
[00:04:06] Sara: typical spikes: 120 concurrent users interacting, average RPS maybe 80, but peak bursts up to 200 for background batch summarization; tokens per request average 320, but can go up to 1,200 in long chart extractions. Daily throughput estimate ~12M tokens.
[00:04:36] Liam: ok that's helpful. So benchmarks we should run: single-request latency at your 320-token average, batched throughput with batch sizes that meet your p95 SLA, and an end-to-end recall/precision eval on your 2k sample notes.

[00:06:00] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: On multilingual: Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese are critical. We also want decent French. Many models are English-first; any suggestions on which open weights perform better for Spanish clinical style?
[00:06:20] Liam: from our previous tests, Mistral-based instruct models show relatively strong non-English fluency out-of-the-box, plus Llama-2-13B-chat variants are surprisingly resilient after LoRA on domain text. Falcon-40B-instruct has strong few-shot but is heavier. For a POC you can try 13B and an 8B Mistral variant plus a 40B baseline — to cover cost/quality spectrum.
[00:06:55] Maya: let's talk shortlist now. We're recommending a three-model shortlist for the POC so you can see tradeoffs: 1) Mistral-Instruct-8B (quantized 4-bit) as a low-cost baseline; 2) Llama-2-13B-chat finetuned with LoRA on your clinical corpus for mid-tier; 3) Falcon-40B-instruct (or similar 34-40B open) as quality upper bound. We'll also propose a smaller instruction-tuned multilingual variant from the Mosaic family as a warm backup.
[00:07:35] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: Why the 13B over a 7B? memory limits aside, we want accuracy and clinical term recall. Wouldn't 7B be cheaper and maybe similar with fine-tune?
[00:07:45] Liam: in our experience, 7B models sometimes drop on long-context dense clinical terminology. You can close the gap with heavy-LoRA or retrieval augmentation, but that adds complexity. The 13B tends to be a good sweet spot for non-English clinical text where model capacity matters.
[00:08:05] Mark: what about quantization — if we do 4-bit q4 or q4o, will that materially change quality for clinical terms?
[00:08:12] Liam: slight degradation in some cases — the KV cache/attn precision can affect rare token recall. But with 4-bit fine-tuned weights and using Redwood's quantization profiles we usually see <1.5% drop on entity recall. We'll include a quant vs fp16 benchmark.

[00:09:30] Maya: procurement and privacy note: you said PHI — do you need private VPC or full on-prem?
[00:09:38] Javier: ideally VPC with customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and audit logs; on-prem is expensive but possible for production. For POC VPC is fine if we can ensure data retention policies.
[00:09:52] Maya: Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC control plane and KMS integration; we can enable log exports for your auditors.

[00:10:30] Liam: for benchmarks — proposed test matrix:
 - Model small (Mistral-8B q4) - cost baseline: measure throughput at batch sizes 1, 4, 8 and p95 latency.
 - Model mid (Llama-2-13B-chat LoRA) - measure accuracy on the 2k eval set, p95/p99 latency in both quantized and fp16 modes.
 - Model large (Falcon-40B-instruct) - measure recall + latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
We'll run these on Redwood Dedicated pool with GPUs similar to your target (A100 or H100 equivalent) and also a Hosted run for comparison.

[00:12:10] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: For the accuracy eval — our rubric focuses on three things: entity recall, medication dosage detection accuracy, and hallucination rate (false positive assertions). Can you run an automated scoring pipeline so we can see detailed failure modes?
[00:12:28] Liam: yes — we'll run the eval scripts you provide and supplement with our prompt-robustness tests. Note: transcription sometimes shows wrong punctuation and casing — the models react, so we'll normalize.

[00:13:00] Mark: timelines — how long to set up Dedicated for the POC and run the suite?
[00:13:06] Maya: typical POC flow we recommend: week 0-1: kickoff + data exchange + infra provisioning; week 2: initial model deploy (Mistral-8B q4) and smoke tests; week 3-4: run accuracy evals and latency benchmarks for 8B and 13B; week 5: Falcon-40B run and cost analysis; week 6: POC recap, decision workshop. So about 6 weeks.
[00:13:32] Sara: that's tight but aligns with procurement needs.

[00:14:00] Liam: about cost: from Redwood side we'll give per-1M token estimates per model and also an estimated Dedicated monthly commit needed to meet your 200 RPS bursts. We'll show how batching and prefix/KV caching reduces token spend.
[00:14:17] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: caching is interesting — can we cache patient-common prefixes? That helps repeated clinician prompts.
[00:14:23] Liam: yes, Redwood supports automatic KV caching and prefix caching; we'll instrument token-level cost savings in the dashboard.

[00:15:05] Maya: any red-lines from compliance?
[00:15:09] Javier: data must be anonymized for POC, until a legal addendum is signed. And encryption keys must be customer-controlled for production.
[00:15:18] Maya: understood.

[00:16:00] (brief cross talk - background noise) Speaker 1: um mm

[00:18:30] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: If we proceed with LoRA, how many tokens do you expect we need for a useful clinical adaptation?
[00:18:38] Liam: typical LoRA on 13B for clinical style: 10k–50k steps on ~100k–300k domain tokens. For small targeted entity calibration you can start with 10k annotated examples = roughly 300k tokens. We'll recommend a staged approach: small LoRA for entity boost first, then broader fine-tune if needed.
[00:19:10] Mark: does Redwood run the fine-tune or do we bring our infra?
[00:19:14] Maya: Redwood can manage fine-tune / LoRA training on Dedicated for the POC (if you allow data in the provisioning), or you can do it in your environment and deliver weights. We support loading LoRA artifacts.

[00:20:00] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: About evaluation, we'll share a labeled 2k subset focused on Spanish clinical notes and a 2k English folder. Can you run language-specific metrics separately?
[00:20:11] Liam: yes we'll split metrics by language and by note type.

[00:21:30] Sara: what about hallucination mitigation — retrieval augmentation or tool calls?
[00:21:36] Liam: retrieval augmentation with a small vector DB populated with your terminologies is effective. Redwood supports also function/tool calling to external clinical knowledge bases. For the POC we can include a retrieval test that compares raw model vs model+retrieval.

[00:23:00] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: Great. Any thoughts on sample prompts? We'll share typical clinician questions.
[00:23:08] Liam: please include both few-shot and one-shot styles — clinical instructions often require strict formats.

[00:25:00] Maya: ok quick note on metrics and acceptance: you mentioned entity recall 92%; what about tolerances? for POC we recommend primary metric = entity recall >= 92% OR > baseline+5%, plus p95 latency < 300ms. If either is met with reasonable cost uplift (<40% vs baseline) you consider pilot.
[00:25:34] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: that seems fair. We also want to quantify hallucination reduction.

[00:27:00] (miss-attribution) Speaker 2: uh right, so

[00:28:10] Liam: technical caveats: for the 40B run we'll need larger GPU instances; p95 will be longer if you insist on fp16. We'll try q4 benchmarks to get nearer to your latency target.
[00:28:35] Mark: do we get tracing and per-token cost breakdown?
[00:28:40] Maya: yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency traces per route and per model; we'll enable you for the POC workspace.

[00:30:00] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: procurement question: will the POC costs be applied to committed Dedicated if we convert?
[00:30:06] Maya: we typically credit a portion of POC charges against an initial committed capacity if you sign a Dedicated contract within agreed terms. We'll include that in the commercial note.

[00:32:00] Sara: what are the failure modes we'll report back as part of the POC deliverable?
[00:32:06] Liam: per-model accuracy breakdown, latency/throughput charts, cost per 1M tokens, suggestions (LoRA vs retrieval), and recommended production architecture (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), plus a risk register.

[00:34:30] Maya: ok let's confirm deliverables and owners (recap):
 - Redwood: share model shortlist + cost estimates + test plan (Maya)
 - Redwood SE: run initial workload smoke and provide Dedicated sizing (Liam)
 - Customer: provide 2k clinical notes + eval rubric (Ana, Sara)
 - Compliance: confirm KMS/SSO requirements (Javier)

[00:38:06] Liam: yes we'll attach anonymized numbers from a similar teladoc-like test (non-PII) showing Llama-13B LoRA often matched a 40B baseline on many clinical recall tasks, but rejection cases remain for rare abbreviations. We'll include that as context.

[00:40:00] Maya: risk calls: if the 13B doesn't meet recall we can iterate LoRA and retrieval in week 4-5, or fallback to 40B for critical flows. We also recommended a canary rollout with automatic fallback to the smaller model if latency spikes.
[00:40:30] Mark: about canary — can Redwood route based on latency policy?
[00:40:34] Liam: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallbacks by policy (latency/cost/region).

[00:42:00] (background typing)

[00:44:00] Sara: outstanding question — what about tokenization differences for Portuguese vs Spanish? we saw some tokenization explosion in a prior test.
[00:44:08] Liam: tokenization can vary; we'll evaluate tokens-per-request for each language and account in cost calc. Some models are more subword-friendly for romance languages.

[00:46:00] Dr. Ana Ribeiro: any advice on prompts that reduce hallucination?
[00:46:07] Liam: constrain the model: explicit system instruction, require citations if info not in the provided text, or return "I don't know" for uncertain facts. We'll test few prompt patterns in the eval.

[00:48:00] Maya: notes for procurement: we'll share SOC 2/ISO paperwork, SSO integration docs, and a template contract clause for keys.
